jane_doe (Customer): hey team — production search started returning 401 invalid_api_key after the 10:09 deploy. customers hitting search in eu-west. quick curl i ran below.

jane_doe (Customer): ```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: ApiKey abcDEF123' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/search?q=test
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not recognized"}
```

jamie (Support): thanks. can you paste the raw request headers from the failing client or a tcpdump? also any x-request-id from the 401 response?

jane_doe (Customer): got the x-request-id from one failed request: req_2026_04_03_1234. full headers from our edge below (sanitized keys):

jane_doe (Customer): ```
Host: api.redwood.example.com
User-Agent: our-client/2.1.0
Authorization: ApiKey abcDEF123, Bearer eyJhbGci...
Accept: application/json
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.1.45
```

jamie (Support): whoa looks like two auth values concatenated (ApiKey + Bearer) in the same header, separated by a comma. runtime expects a single prefix/value. tagging eng oncall @ryan, infra-bot please pull logs for req_2026_04_03_1234 :eyes:

infra-bot: pulled logs for req_2026_04_03_1234 — auth failure: invalid_api_key. upstream proxy inserted an Authorization header with Bearer token. Log excerpt: `auth: header contains multiple values; rejecting`

ryan (Eng Oncall): confirmed. we replicate locally:

ryan (Eng Oncall): ```bash
# works (single ApiKey)
curl -s -H 'Authorization: ApiKey goodkey' https://api-redwood/local/v1/ping | jq .
# 200 ok

# broken (comma-concatenated)
curl -s -H 'Authorization: ApiKey goodkey, Bearer foobar' https://api-redwood/local/v1/ping | jq .
# 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

ryan (Eng Oncall): server-side auth parser treats the header as a single token string; a comma or extra token breaks validation. The proxy in front of our edge is adding a Bearer header for internal tracing and appends rather than replacing, which created a combined header value.

jamie (Support): what are remediation steps? customer is worried the key leaked since the header contains a Bearer jwt.

ryan (Eng Oncall): two things: short-term, ask the client to switch to X-Api-Key (custom header) or ensure their client sends only the ApiKey header (no comma). Longer-term, infra needs to change the proxy to replace Authorization rather than append, and scrub headers when logging. For security, rotate the exposed API key and blacklist the old one.

jamie (Support): jane_doe — could you try a quick smoke with X-Api-Key to confirm? if that works we'll guide infra and rotate keys.

jane_doe (Customer): trying now...

jane_doe (Customer): ```bash
curl -i -H 'X-Api-Key: abcDEF123' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/search?q=test
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"results":[] }
```

jamie (Support): nice — so path forward: 1) infra to patch proxy config to not append Authorization (ryan/infra), 2) customer rotates the key (jamie to coordinate), 3) if jwt leaked, rotate that too and check logs for exposure. I'll open an internal ticket to track. :thumbsup:

ryan (Eng Oncall): created internal ticket INF-4821 to update proxy rewrite rules and add header scrubbing in logs. Estimated fix in next deploy window.

jamie (Support): jane_doe — do you want us to rotate the API key from our side or will you rotate? We can also issue a temporary key immediately.

jane_doe (Customer): please rotate from your side and provide the new key. also confirm the old key is revoked.

jamie (Support): done — rotated key, sent new key to your org admin via secure channel, revoked old key (old key id key_2026_eu_07). please test and confirm when ready.

jane_doe (Customer): confirmed tests passing with new key. thanks all. closing ticket once infra deploys the proxy fix.

ryan (Eng Oncall): leaving a note: consider accepting multiple auth header formats in the future or returning a clearer error when header contains commas, to help troubleshooting.

jamie (Support): noted. marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
